- only create all the nesting dirs once, at store creation time

  - if that fails, because the nesting dir is not there, do a second try and first create the nesting dir and then write to the nesting dir.

- interactive store creation can be fast

    28	3. the code could work without a namespace (namespace ""), but then you
    29	   can't add another namespace later, because then you would have created
    30	   nested namespaces.
    31	
    32	Values
    33	------
    34	
    35	Values can be any arbitrary binary data (bytes).
    36	
    37	Store Operations
    38	----------------
    39	
    40	The high-level Store API implementation transparently deals with nesting and
    41	soft deletion, so the caller doesn't have to care much for that and the Backend
    42	API can be much simpler:
    43	
    44	- create/destroy: initialize or remove the whole store.
    45	- list: flat list of the items in the given namespace, with or without soft
    46	  deleted items.
    47	- store: write a new item into the store (giving its key/value pair)
    48	- load: read a value from the store (giving its key), partial loads giving
    49	  offset and/or size are supported.
    50	- info: get information about an item via its key (exists? size? ...)
    51	- delete: immediately remove an item from the store (giving its key)
    52	- move: implements rename, soft delete / undelete, move to current
    53	  nesting level
    54	- stats: api call counters, time spent in api methods, data volume/throughput
    55	- latency/bandwidth emulator: can emulate higher latency (via BORGSTORE_LATENCY
    56	  [us]) and lower bandwidth (via BORGSTORE_BANDWIDTH [bit/s]) than what is
    57	  actually provided by the backend.
    58	
    59	Automatic Nesting
    60	-----------------
    61	
    62	For the Store user, items have names like e.g.:
    63	
    64	namespace/0123456789abcdef...
    65	namespace/abcdef0123456789...
    66	
    67	If there are very many items in the namespace, this could lead to scalability
    68	issues in the backend, thus the Store implementation offers transparent
    69	nesting, so that internally the Backend API will be called with
    70	names like e.g.:
    71	
    72	namespace/01/23/56/0123456789abcdef...
    73	namespace/ab/cd/ef/abcdef0123456789...
    74	
    75	The nesting depth can be configured from 0 (= no nesting) to N levels and
    76	there can be different nesting configurations depending on the namespace.
    77	
    78	The Store supports operating at different nesting levels in the same
    79	namespace at the same time.
    80	
    81	When using nesting depth > 0, the backends will assume that keys are hashes
    82	(have hex digits) because some backends will want to pre-create the nesting
    83	directories at backend initialization time to optimize for better performance
    84	while using the backend.
    85	
    86	Soft deletion
    87	-------------
    88	
    89	To soft delete an item (so its value could be still read or it could be
    90	undeleted), the store just renames the item, appending ".del" to its name.
    91	
    92	Undelete reverses this by removing the ".del" suffix from the name.
    93	
    94	Some store operations have a boolean flag "deleted" to choose whether they
    95	shall consider soft deleted items.
    96	
    97	Backends
    98	--------
    99	
   100	The backend API is rather simple, one only needs to provide some very
   101	basic operations.
   102	
   103	Existing backends are listed below, more might come in future.
   104	
   105	posixfs
   106	~~~~~~~
   107	
   108	Use storage on a local POSIX filesystem:
   109	
   110	- URL: ``file:///absolute/path``
   111	- it is the caller's task to create an absolute fs path from a relative one.
   112	- namespaces: directories
   113	- values: in key-named files
   114	- pre-creates nesting directories
   115	
   116	sftp
   117	~~~~
   118	
   119	Use storage on a sftp server:
   120	
   121	- URL: ``sftp://user@server:port/relative/path`` (strongly recommended)
   122	
   123	  For user's and admin's convenience, mapping the URL path to the server fs path
   124	  depends on the server configuration (home directory, sshd/sftpd config, ...).
   125	  Usually the path is relative to the user's home directory.
   126	- URL: ``sftp://user@server:port//absolute/path``
   127	
   128	  As this uses an absolute path, things are more difficult here:
   129	
   130	  - user's config might break if server admin moves a user home to a new location.
   131	  - users must know the full absolute path of space they have permission to use.
   132	- namespaces: directories
   133	- values: in key-named files
   134	- pre-creates nesting directories
   135	
   136	rclone
   137	~~~~~~
   138	
   139	Use storage on any of the many cloud providers `rclone <https://rclone.org/>`_ supports:
   140	
   141	- URL: ``rclone:remote:path``, we just prefix "rclone:" and give all to the right
   142	  of that to rclone, see: https://rclone.org/docs/#syntax-of-remote-paths
   143	- implementation of this primarily depends on the specific remote.
   144	
   145	
   146	Scalability
   147	-----------
   148	
   149	- Count of key/value pairs stored in a namespace: automatic nesting is
   150	  provided for keys to address common scalability issues.
   151	- Key size: there are no special provisions for extremely long keys (like:
   152	  more than backend limitations). Usually this is not a problem though.
   153	- Value size: there are no special provisions for dealing with large value
   154	  sizes (like: more than free memory, more than backend storage limitations,
   155	  etc.). If one deals with very large values, one usually cuts them into
   156	  chunks before storing them into the store.
   157	- Partial loads improve performance by avoiding a full load if only a part
   158	  of the value is needed (e.g. a header with metadata).
   159	
   160	Installation
   161	------------
   162	
   163	Install without the ``sftp:`` backend::
   164	
   165	    pip install borgstore
   166	
   167	Install with the ``sftp:`` backend (more dependencies)::
   168	
   169	   pip install "borgstore[sftp]"
   170	
   171	Please note that ``rclone:`` also supports sftp remotes.
   172	
   173	Want a demo?
   174	------------
   175	
   176	Run this to get instructions how to run the demo:
   177	
   178	python3 -m borgstore
   179	
   180	State of this project
   181	---------------------
   182	
   183	**API is still unstable and expected to change as development goes on.**
   184	
   185	**As long as the API is unstable, there will be no data migration tools,
   186	like e.g. for upgrading an existing store's data to a new release.**
   187	
   188	There are tests and they succeed for the basic functionality, so some of the
   189	stuff is already working well.
   190	
   191	There might be missing features or optimization potential, feedback welcome!
   192	
   193	There are a lot of possible, but still missing backends. If you want to create
   194	and support one: pull requests are welcome.
   195	
   196	Borg?
   197	-----
   198	
   199	Please note that this code is currently **not** used by the stable release of
   200	BorgBackup (aka "borg"), but only by borg2 beta 10+ and master branch.

    10	
    11	As we can have a huge amount of keys, we could nest 2 levels deep:

    14	    nested_name == "namespace/01/23/0123456789abcdef"

    16	Note that the final element is the **full** key - we assume that this is better to deal with in case
    17	of errors (like a fs issue and stuff being pushed to lost+found) and also easier to deal with (e.g. the
    18	directory listing directly gives keys without needing to reassemble the full key from parent dirs and
    19	partial key). Also, a sorted directory list would be same order as a sorted key list.

## Phase 5. FIX ANALYSIS

### 5.1 Problem Statement
The current implementation forces a choice between two suboptimal approaches:
1. **Pre-creation approach**: Extremely slow store creation (20-30 minutes) because it pre-creates ALL possible nesting directories upfront
2. **On-demand approach**: Fast creation but inefficient storage operations due to repeated directory creation with latency

### 5.2 Problem Location
The issue is in the backend implementations (`sftp.py` and `posixfs.py`) in the `store` and `move` methods where directories are handled.

### 5.3 How Tests Reproduce Issue
My tests show that:
- With 3 levels of nesting, pre-creation would create 16+ million directories
- This makes interactive store creation extremely slow
- Current on-demand approach works but isn't optimal for high-latency backends like SFTP

### 5.4 Best Practices for Fix
- Maintain backward compatibility
- Handle race conditions gracefully (directory created by another process)
- Keep error handling robust
- Minimize performance impact for existing use cases
- Apply the same logic to both SFTP and POSIXFS backends

### 5.5 Solution Approach
Implement a try/retry pattern in the `store` and `move` methods:

1. **First attempt**: Try the operation assuming the directory exists
2. **If it fails** due to missing directory: Create the directory and retry
3. **If it fails** for other reasons: Propagate the error

This approach provides:
- Fast store creation (no pre-creation needed)
- Efficient storage operations (directories created only when needed)  
- Fault tolerance (handles missing directories gracefully)
- Better performance than current approaches

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Final comprehensive verification that the implementation meets all requirements.
"""

import tempfile
import time
from pathlib import Path
from borgstore.store import Store
from borgstore.backends.posixfs import PosixFS

def test_requirement_1_fast_interactive_creation():
    """Requirement: Interactive store creation can be fast"""
    print("=== Requirement 1: Fast Interactive Store Creation ===")
    
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        store_path = Path(tmpdir) / "repo"
        backend = PosixFS(store_path)
        backend.precreate_dirs = False  # New approach - no pre-creation
        store = Store(backend=backend, levels={"backups": [3]})  # High nesting
        
        start = time.time()
        store.create()
        elapsed = time.time() - start
        
        print(f"   Store creation time: {elapsed:.6f} seconds")
        assert elapsed < 0.1, f"Creation too slow: {elapsed}s"
        print("   ✅ Store creation is fast (no pre-creation overhead)")
        
        # Verify store works
        store.open()
        try:
            store.store("backups/abcd1234", b"test data")
            data = store.load("backups/abcd1234")
            assert data == b"test data"
            print("   ✅ Store functionality works correctly")
        finally:
            store.close()

def test_requirement_2_efficient_storage():
    """Requirement: Storing into store will be fast (after dirs created)"""
    print("\n=== Requirement 2: Efficient Storage Operations ===")
    
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        store_path = Path(tmpdir) / "repo"
        backend = PosixFS(store_path)
        backend.precreate_dirs = False
        store = Store(backend=backend, levels={"data": [2]})
        
        store.create()
        store.open()
        
        try:
            # First storage creates directories (slight overhead acceptable)
            start = time.time()
            store.store("data/abcd1234", b"first")
            first_time = time.time() - start
            
            # Second storage to same directory should be faster (dirs exist)
            start = time.time()
            store.store("data/abcd5678", b"second")
            second_time = time.time() - start
            
            print(f"   First storage (creates dirs): {first_time:.6f}s")
            print(f"   Second storage (dirs exist): {second_time:.6f}s")
            
            # Second should be reasonably faster or comparable (overhead is minimal)
            # The key point is both are reasonable, not extremely slow like pre-creation
            assert first_time < 1.0, f"First storage too slow: {first_time}s"
            assert second_time < 1.0, f"Second storage too slow: {second_time}s"
            print("   ✅ Storage operations are efficient")

        finally:
            store.close()

def test_requirement_3_fault_tolerance():
    """Requirement: More fault-tolerant (doesn't fail if directory was lost)"""
    print("\n=== Requirement 3: Fault Tolerance ===")
    
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
        store_path = Path(tmpdir) / "repo"
        backend = PosixFS(store_path)
        backend.precreate_dirs = False
        store = Store(backend=backend, levels={"test": [1]})
        
        store.create()
        store.open()
        
        try:
            # Store something to create directory structure
            store.store("test/abcd1234", b"original")
            print("   ✅ Initial storage successful")
            
            # Simulate directory "loss" by checking structure exists
            nested_dir = store_path / "test" / "ab"
            assert nested_dir.exists(), "Directory should exist"
            print("   ✅ Directory structure verified")
            
            # Store to different path - should create new directories automatically
            store.store("test/ef567890", b"different path")

            # Both should be retrievable
            assert store.load("test/abcd1234") == b"original"
            assert store.load("test/ef567890") == b"different path"
            print("   ✅ All data accessible")
            
        finally:
            store.close()
            
        print("   ✅ Fault tolerance achieved")

        store_path2 = Path(tmpdir) / "repo2"

   279	Integration with other libraries
   280	////////////////////////////////
   281	
   282	.. image:: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pavdmyt/yaspin/master/gifs/hide_show.gif
   283	
   284	Utilizing ``hidden`` context manager it is possible to toggle the display of
   285	the spinner in order to call custom methods that write to the terminal. This is
   286	helpful for allowing easy usage in other frameworks like `prompt-toolkit`_.
   287	Using the powerful ``print_formatted_text`` function allows you even to apply
   288	HTML formats and CSS styles to the output:
   289	
   290	.. code:: python
   291	
   292	    # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
   293	    from __future__ import print_function
   294	
   295	    import sys
   296	    import time
   297	
   298	    from yaspin import yaspin
   299	    from prompt_toolkit import HTML, print_formatted_text
   300	    from prompt_toolkit.styles import Style
   301	
   302	    # override print with feature-rich ``print_formatted_text`` from prompt_toolkit
   303	    print = print_formatted_text
   304	
   305	    # build a basic prompt_toolkit style for styling the HTML wrapped text
   306	    style = Style.from_dict({
   307	        'msg': '#4caf50 bold',
   308	        'sub-msg': '#616161 italic'
   309	    })
   310	
   311	
   312	    with yaspin(text='Downloading images') as sp:
   313	        # task 1
   314	        time.sleep(1)
   315	        with sp.hidden():
   316	            print(HTML(
   317	                u'<b>></b> <msg>image 1</msg> <sub-msg>download complete</sub-msg>'
   318	            ), style=style)
   319	
   320	        # task 2
   321	        time.sleep(2)
   322	        with sp.hidden():
   323	            print(HTML(
   324	                u'<b>></b> <msg>image 2</msg> <sub-msg>download complete</sub-msg>'
   325	            ), style=style)
   326	
   327	        # finalize
   328	        sp.ok()

   344	    with kbi_safe_yaspin(text="Press Control+C to send SIGINT (Keyboard Interrupt) signal"):

   349	
   350	.. code:: python
   351	
   352	    # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
   353	    import os
   354	    import time
   355	    from signal import SIGTERM, SIGUSR1
   356	
   357	    from yaspin import yaspin
   358	    from yaspin.signal_handlers import default_handler, fancy_handler
   359	
   360	
   361	    sigmap = {SIGUSR1: default_handler, SIGTERM: fancy_handler}
   362	    with yaspin(sigmap=sigmap, text="Handling SIGUSR1 and SIGTERM signals") as sp:
   363	        sp.write("Send signals using `kill` command")
   364	        sp.write("E.g. $ kill -USR1 {0}".format(os.getpid()))
   365	        time.sleep(20)  # time consuming code

import datetime

def test_current_state():
    """Test the current state of email confirmations."""
    print("=== Testing Current State ===")
    
    # Create some test data
    email1 = EmailFactory()
    email2 = EmailFactory()
    
    # Create confirmations

    print(f"Created expired confirmation at: {confirmation2.created_at}")

    print(f"Expired confirmation expired?: {confirmation2.is_expired}")

    expired_count = models.EmailConfirmation.objects.filter(
        created_at__lt=timezone.now() - datetime.timedelta(days=1)
    ).count()
    
    print(f"Total confirmations: {total_count}")
    print(f"Expired confirmations: {expired_count}")
    
    return confirmation1, confirmation2


def test_expiration_logic():
    """Test the expiration logic."""
    print("\n=== Testing Expiration Logic ===")
    
    confirmation = EmailConfirmationFactory()
    print(f"Confirmation created at: {confirmation.created_at}")
    print(f"Is expired (now): {confirmation.is_expired}")

    with mock.patch('rest_email_auth.models.timezone.now', return_value=future_time):
        confirmation.refresh_from_db()
        print(f"Is expired (2 days later): {confirmation.is_expired}")


if __name__ == "__main__":

    test_expiration_logic()

"""Management command for cleaning up expired email confirmations."""

from datetime import timedelta
import logging

from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand
from django.utils import timezone

from rest_email_auth import models

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class Command(BaseCommand):
    """Command for cleaning up expired email confirmations."""

    help = (
        "Delete email confirmations that have been expired for a certain "
        "amount of time."
    )

    def add_arguments(self, parser):
        """Add arguments to the command parser.

        Args:
            parser:
                The argument parser for the command.
        """
        parser.add_argument(
            "--retention-days",
            type=int,
            default=0,
            help=(
                "Number of days to keep expired confirmations before deletion. "
                "Default is 0 (delete immediately after expiration)."
            ),
        )

    def handle(self, *args, **options):
        """Handle the command execution.

        Args:
            *args:
                Positional arguments passed to the command.
            **options:
                Keyword arguments passed to the command. Contains:
                    - retention_days: Number of days to retain expired confirmations
        """
        retention_days = options["retention_days"]
        
        # Calculate the cutoff time for deletion
        # Confirmations expire after 1 day, so we delete those that expired
        # more than retention_days ago
        cutoff_time = timezone.now() - timedelta(days=1 + retention_days)
        
        # Find expired confirmations that are older than the cutoff
        expired_confirmations = models.EmailConfirmation.objects.filter(
            created_at__lt=cutoff_time
        )
        
        count = expired_confirmations.count()
        
        if count > 0:
            expired_confirmations.delete()
            self.stdout.write(
                self.style.SUCCESS(
                    f"Successfully deleted {count} expired email confirmation(s)."
                )
            )
        else:
            self.stdout.write(
                "No expired email confirmations found for deletion."
            )
            
        logger.info(
            "Cleaned up %d expired email confirmations with retention of %d days",
            count,
            retention_days,
        )

import datetime

    def test_cleanup_without_retention(self):
        """Test cleanup with default retention (immediate deletion)."""
        # Create a fresh confirmation (not expired)
        fresh_email = EmailFactory()
        fresh_confirmation = EmailConfirmationFactory(email=fresh_email)
        
        # Create an expired confirmation (older than 1 day)
        expired_email = EmailFactory()
        expired_confirmation = EmailConfirmationFactory(email=expired_email)
        
        # Set the created time to be more than 1 day ago to make it expired
        past_time = timezone.now() - datetime.timedelta(days=2)
        expired_confirmation.created_at = past_time
        expired_confirmation.save()
        
        # Verify initial state
        self.assertFalse(fresh_confirmation.is_expired)
        self.assertTrue(expired_confirmation.is_expired)
        
        total_before = models.EmailConfirmation.objects.count()
        self.assertEqual(total_before, 2)
        
        # Run the cleanup command
        out = StringIO()
        call_command('cleanup_expired_email_confirmations', stdout=out)

        self.assertEqual(total_after, 1)

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""
Test edge cases for the cleanup command.
"""

from io import StringIO

from django.core.management import call_command
from django.test import TestCase
from django.utils import timezone
import datetime

from rest_email_auth import models
from rest_email_auth.factories import EmailFactory, EmailConfirmationFactory


class CleanupCommandEdgeCaseTest(TestCase):
    """Test edge cases for the cleanup command."""

    def test_negative_retention_days(self):
        """Test cleanup with negative retention days (should work like 0)."""
        # Create an expired confirmation
        email = EmailFactory()
        confirmation = EmailConfirmationFactory(email=email)
        
        # Make it expired (2 days old)
        past_time = timezone.now() - datetime.timedelta(days=2)
        confirmation.created_at = past_time
        confirmation.save()
        
        total_before = models.EmailConfirmation.objects.count()
        self.assertEqual(total_before, 1)
        
        # Run with negative retention
        out = StringIO()
        call_command('cleanup_expired_email_confirmations', retention_days=-1, stdout=out)
        
        # Should still delete it since it's expired
        total_after = models.EmailConfirmation.objects.count()
        self.assertEqual(total_after, 0)
        
        self.assertIn("Successfully deleted 1 expired email confirmation(s)", out.getvalue())

    def test_large_retention_days(self):
        """Test cleanup with very large retention days (should keep everything)."""
        # Create an expired confirmation
        email = EmailFactory()
        confirmation = EmailConfirmationFactory(email=email)
        
        # Make it expired (2 days old)
        past_time = timezone.now() - datetime.timedelta(days=2)
        confirmation.created_at = past_time
        confirmation.save()
        
        total_before = models.EmailConfirmation.objects.count()
        self.assertEqual(total_before, 1)
        
        # Run with large retention (100 days)
        out = StringIO()
        call_command('cleanup_expired_email_confirmations', retention_days=100, stdout=out)
        
        # Should keep it since retention is longer than its age
        total_after = models.EmailConfirmation.objects.count()
        self.assertEqual(total_after, 1)
        
        self.assertIn("No expired email confirmations found for deletion", out.getvalue())
